tasks.name: Build Value Roadmap
tasks.purpose: Sequence the business outcomes and value targets into a delivery roadmap — the time-phased commitment of *which outcomes are realised when*. The roadmap is the artefact the sponsor signs and the single reference for how Delivery Loops will be ordered and how value is monitored in Deploy.

tasks.name: Define High-Level Scope
tasks.purpose: Define the engagement boundaries at a level sufficient to drive the value case and to frame Foundation. Captures what is in scope, what is explicitly out, what geographies, legal entities, business domains, and integration boundaries apply, and the assumptions that bound the scope.
outputs: In-scope business domains, end-to-end processes, geographies, and legal entities
Row-level originating capability references or context-origin: none justification

tasks.name: Run Value Case Sign-Off
tasks.purpose: Gate the Process and Value phase. Review every context artefact produced in this phase against the phase exit criteria, secure executive sign-off, and formally close Process and Value so Foundation can start.

tasks.name: Build Business Value Plan
tasks.purpose: The Process and Value phase establishes *what* value the engagement is expected to deliver — business outcomes carrying stable `BO#` IDs, quantified value targets, and a sequenced value roadmap. None of that says *how* the value will be measured, who is accountable for measuring it, or how a shortfall is detected while there is still time to act. The Business Value Management Plan closes that gap: it is the framework for measuring, monitoring, and controlling realisation of the expected business value, and for integrating that framework into the programme's own management and governance.
outputs: Business value definitions, assumptions, and how each value will be realised
Outcome → programme component → business value linkage
The business value measurement framework (measure, baseline, target, method, frequency, data source)
The performance baseline established against that framework
The business value risk and opportunity assessment, with response strategies
Roles and responsibilities in the execution of value management
The approach for transitioning benefits to operations
Governance of the value management process

tasks.name: Assess Governance Maturity
tasks.purpose: Evaluate the completeness and quality of all Foundation governance artefacts before the engagement transitions into Delivery Loops. This assessment acts as the Foundation phase gate for the Transformation stream — confirming that the governance baseline is in place, identifying gaps or weaknesses, and producing a maturity score with remediation actions. Without this gate, the engagement risks entering iterative delivery with incomplete governance structures.

tasks.name: Baseline Program Financials
tasks.purpose: Establish the financial baseline for the engagement — the approved budget, cost allocation by workstream and phase, ECIF/consumption targets, and the forecast that will be tracked against actuals throughout Delivery Loops. This artefact creates the single financial reference point for variance analysis, change control (cost impact of CRs), and financial close-out at Deploy.

tasks.name: Build General Approach
tasks.purpose: Produce a **General Approach** — an optional, high-level document that explains *how* the engagement will deliver its target: an AI use case, or a more complex capability in Dynamics 365. It sets out the phased shape of the delivery (from mobilisation through foundation to delivery loops and deploy), the key activities, outcomes and workshops per phase, the governance that runs in parallel, the iteration timeline with its milestones and decision points, and the team and roles that deliver it.

tasks.name: Build Resource Plan
tasks.purpose: Produce a Resource / Staffing Plan that defines who is needed, when, with what skills, and how they will be onboarded and offboarded throughout the engagement. This artefact operationalises the team structure from the Stakeholder & Team Context into a time-phased staffing plan with GRM requests, ramp up/down schedules, and onboarding procedures. It feeds the Program Roadmap (resource-driven scheduling), Financial Baseline (cost allocation), and is actively managed through Delivery Loops via the Resource / Staffing Monitoring capability.

tasks.name: Generate Scope Breakdown
tasks.purpose: Produce a structured scope breakdown document that translates the Solution stream's scope context (Epics, Features, User Stories) into a governance-grade view of what is in scope, what is out of scope, key assumptions, constraints, and WBS boundaries. This deliverable is consumed by downstream Transformation deliverables (Project Charter, Program Roadmap, Resource Plan, Financial Baseline) and serves as the authoritative scope reference for governance reviews, change control, and stakeholder alignment.
outputs: Governance-grade document detailing in-scope items, out-of-scope items, assumptions, constraints, and deferred items
Serves as the authoritative scope reference for change control and governance reviews throughout delivery

tasks.name: Generate Stakeholder Map
tasks.purpose: Produce a prioritised stakeholder map with interest × impact classification, RACI assignments, and a stakeholder engagement strategy. This artefact transforms the Stakeholder Context into a governance-grade output consumed by the Governance Model, Communications Plan, and Status Reporting cadence. It also incorporates the Value-Owning Stakeholders identified during Process and Value (presales).

tasks.name: Identify Refinement Actions
tasks.purpose: Translate the gaps and weaknesses identified in the Governance Maturity Assessment into a prioritised, actionable remediation plan. This task closes the Foundation loop — feeding evaluation results back into concrete actions that must be completed before or during Delivery Loops to bring governance to the required maturity level.

tasks.name: Produce Project Charter
tasks.purpose: Produce a Project Charter and Kick-off Deck that formally establishes the engagement — its business outcomes, scope, governance structure, team, schedule, and success criteria. This artefact is the single reference for what the project is, why it exists, and how it will be governed. It anchors the customer kick-off meeting and serves as the baseline for all downstream governance artefacts.
outputs: Risk Management Plan / Initial RAID Log

tasks.name: Build Backlog
tasks.purpose: Materialise and maintain the delivery backlog: the committed, prioritised units of work the team will build, each tracing back to a capability in the context plane. This is the task that turns *what we know* (use cases and capabilities, in context) into *what we will build* (Epics, Features, and User Stories, in state).
outputs: The Epic → Feature → User Story work-item tree in state/backlog/, as flat files with parent
The Backlog register in state/index.md, listing every Epic, Feature, and User Story with type,
The matching work items in the tracker, with system-of-record and external-ref recorded on
An appended state/log.md entry for every create, promote, transition, re-prioritisation, and drop

tasks.name: Build Capability Catalogue (gaps)
tasks.purpose: The Capability Catalogue is a structured inventory of every capability the target solution must deliver — mapped against the platform's standard capabilities and flagged where gaps exist. It translates the Reference Process Model into a capability-level view: what the platform can do out-of-box, what needs configuration, and what represents a genuine gap requiring extension, customisation, or an ISV solution. This catalogue feeds the Fit/Gap Register with pre-classified gaps and gives the Solution Architect a single view of solution coverage.

tasks.name: Build Delivery IP Inventory
tasks.purpose: The Delivery IP Inventory identifies and catalogues all reusable intellectual property available to accelerate the engagement — accelerators, templates, connectors, reference implementations, ISV solutions, and AI skills from the Knowledge Garden, DRIVE catalogue, and central repository. The inventory prevents reinventing what already exists and ensures the team starts sprints with the best available starting points. It also surfaces contribution-back opportunities where new IP created during the engagement can be shared with the wider organisation.
outputs: Source (Knowledge Garden / DRIVE / Central Repo / ISV)

tasks.name: Build Fit/Gap Register
tasks.purpose: The Fit/Gap Register systematically compares every in-scope business process from the Reference Process Model against the target platform's standard capabilities (D365, Power Platform, M365, or AI/agent capabilities depending on archetype). Each gap is classified by resolution approach — Configure, Extend, Customise, ISV, or Workaround. This register becomes the primary input for estimating customisation effort, planning Config & Dev sprints, and governing scope through ARB/CCB reviews.
outputs: Gap Type (Configure / Extend / Customise / ISV / Workaround)

tasks.name: Build Integration Architecture Blueprint
tasks.purpose: Produce the Integration Architecture Blueprint — a dedicated deliverable that details every integration point, interface contract, middleware layer, and data exchange pattern between the solution and external systems. While the Initial Solution Architecture identifies integration points at a high level and the SDD captures integration design per business process area, the Blueprint is the single authoritative reference for the integration landscape as a whole: system inventory, interface catalogue, protocol and transport decisions, error-handling patterns, monitoring approach, and the environment-specific topology. It is the primary input for the Delivery Loops integration build and the basis for integration testing scope.
outputs: Published to the project repository and linked from the project wiki

tasks.name: Build Solution Design Document
tasks.purpose: Produce the Solution Design Document (SDD) — the comprehensive design record that translates the Initial Solution Architecture into detailed functional and technical design per business process area. The SDD captures how each requirement will be fulfilled (fit, gap, extension, customisation), the configuration approach, integration design, data model, security model, and agentic/AI component design where applicable. It is the primary reference for the Build phase and the single document that connects the backlog (Epics, Features, User Stories), the reference process model, and the capability landscape into a buildable design. During Delivery Loops, the SDD is iteratively updated as design decisions are validated, refined, or changed through ARB/CCB reviews.
outputs: Functional design per business process area
Published to the project repository, linked from the project wiki, and baselined as v1.0 for Delivery Loops to build against

tasks.name: Build Solution Prototype
tasks.purpose: The Solution Prototype is a working, demonstrable system that proves the most transformative business processes can be realised on the target platform. It validates the Solution Design Document against reality — showing stakeholders what the solution will look and feel like before full build begins. The prototype establishes the baseline configuration and data model definitions that Config & Dev sprints build upon, and surfaces design gaps early when they are cheapest to fix.
outputs: Working prototype environment with baseline configuration, data model definitions, and 3–5 end-to-end business processes demonstrable to the customer
Accompanied by a demo deck, a walkthrough script, and a prototype feedback log capturing stakeholder reactions and change requests

tasks.name: Create Initial Solution Architecture
tasks.purpose: Produce an initial solution architecture that provides a high-level view of the complete solution landscape — application components, integration points, data flows, infrastructure topology, ISV products, and agentic/AI components where applicable. This is the first committed architectural deliverable in Foundation and becomes the structural frame that the Solution Design Document (SDD), Integration Architecture Blueprint, and all Delivery Loops build activities reference. The architecture synthesises everything the Foundation context tasks have captured — scope, requirements, legal constraints, country variations, and the reference process model — into a coherent technical picture of what will be built.
outputs: Published to the project repository and linked from the project wiki

tasks.name: Create Reference Process Model
tasks.purpose: Produce a reference process model that maps the customer's in-scope business processes to the platform's out-of-box (OOB) process catalogue. The model structures processes in a three-level hierarchy — area → end-to-end process → sub-process — and becomes the shared baseline that the Capability Catalogue (gap analysis), Fit/Gap Register, Solution Design Document, and Delivery Loops build activities all draw from. For Pure Business Solution and Hybrid archetypes, the reference model is anchored to the Microsoft Dynamics 365 business process catalogue; the customer's terminology and process variations are layered on top.
outputs: A self-contained document mapping the customer's in-scope business processes to the platform's reference process catalogue in a three-level hierarchy (area → end-to-end process → sub-process), with customer terminology, process scenarios, and front-matter metadata
Published to the project repository and linked from the project wiki

tasks.name: Create Workshop Agenda
tasks.purpose: The Workshop Plan says *which* workshops run, when, and why. It does not say how a single workshop is actually run. The Workshop Agenda closes that gap: for **one** scheduled workshop it produces the timeboxed run sheet the facilitator works from — each session with a start time, a duration, a format (present, walkthrough, whiteboard, demo, decide), a named owner, and the specific in-scope material it covers.
inputs: Workshop Plan entry (objective, expected outcome, date, duration, mode)
outputs: Workshop identifier, title, date, duration, and delivery mode
Objective and the expected outcome it feeds
Roles: facilitator, scribe, decision maker(s), and required attendees
Decisions to land and the questions each session must answer
Pre-work required from the customer and from the delivery team
Materials, demo environments, and sample data required
Follow-ups and the handover into the downstream Solution outcome

tasks.name: Define Country and Legal Scope
tasks.purpose: Capture the two scope dimensions that sit alongside functional scope and constrain it: **where** the solution is rolled out, and **what law and regulation require of it**.
outputs: Country and localisation scope rows in state/scope/, each carrying:
localisation attributes (language, currency, tax, accounting, regulatory)
Legal and regulatory scope rows in the same register, each carrying:
category (data protection / financial / industry / accessibility / AI governance)
the concrete solution requirement it translates into
the Feature(s) it constrains, or a recorded gap where it has none
Row-level originating capability references, or a row-level context-origin: none justification
Updated registers in state/index.md and an appended state/log.md entry

tasks.name: Define Cutover Strategy
tasks.purpose: Define the cutover strategy — the end-to-end go-live approach covering all streams and dimensions: environment readiness, data migration sequencing, integration switchover, ACM (Adoption, Change & Service Management), security and access provisioning, AI/agent activation, rollback strategy, freeze windows, communications, and hypercare model. The strategy is the "conductor's score" that will be refined through Delivery Loops and executed in Deploy.

tasks.name: Define Data Migration Strategy
tasks.purpose: Define the end-to-end data migration strategy — identifying data domains (master, transactional, reference, historical), defining migration scope per phase (what migrates when, what never migrates), agreeing on data ownership (business vs IT), assessing data quality risks, and deciding the migration approach (big-bang vs phased, full vs delta). The strategy ensures the team has a clear, testable, repeatable migration plan before Delivery Loops begin building pipelines. The Data stream owns the technical data model and quality; the Solution stream owns the migration approach, scope sequencing, and business acceptance.
outputs: Prioritised migration backlog ready for Delivery Loops

tasks.name: Define Reporting & Analytics Strategy
tasks.purpose: Define the reporting and analytics strategy — identifying what business reports, dashboards, KPIs, and self-service analytics the solution must deliver, selecting the tooling (Power BI, embedded dashboards, Dataverse views), designing the analytics data model, and planning the delivery approach (managed vs self-service, refresh cadence, security). KPIs must tie back to the Value stream's business objectives and value targets so reporting directly measures business value realisation.

tasks.name: Define Test Strategy
tasks.purpose: Produce the Test Strategy — the overarching test planning deliverable that defines how the solution will be verified and validated across every testing type, environment, and release. The Test Strategy establishes the test approach and methodologies, testing scope (in/out per test type), test cycles and their alignment to Delivery Loops, entry/exit criteria per test type, environment requirements, test data strategy, defect management process, roles and responsibilities, and quality gates. It is produced in Foundation so that Delivery Loops can execute testing from the first sprint against an agreed framework. The strategy covers functional testing (process tests, E2E/SIT), non-functional testing (performance, security, accessibility), user acceptance testing (UAT), and — for agentic archetypes — AI-specific testing (back-testing, usability testing, guardrail validation).
outputs: Test cycle plan aligned to Delivery Loops
Published to the project repository and linked from the project wiki

tasks.name: Generate Workshop Plan
tasks.purpose: At the start of an engagement, a series of workshops is run to understand the solution the customer is looking for and to demonstrate candidate solutions built on Dynamics 365, Copilot agents, Azure Foundry, and other Microsoft technologies. The Workshop Plan is the artefact that aligns the customer and the delivery team on the timeline, the expected participants, the agendas, and the intended outcomes of those workshops before they begin.
outputs: Participants (customer and Microsoft) and their roles
Date, time, duration, and location / delivery mode
Prerequisites, materials, and demo assets required
Owner (Responsible) and tracking link (e.g. ADO work item)

tasks.name: Build Initial Pipeline Skeleton
tasks.purpose: Build and run the first working end-to-end pipeline — build, test, package, deploy to the first non-prod ring — against the Pipeline Architecture, Branching Strategy, Target Environment Topology, Quality Gates & Observability and Secrets & Config Management Approach. The skeleton is the proof-of-implementation: Foundation design becomes executable code. Its first-run telemetry feeds directly into the CD Readiness Review and any refinement that surfaces.
outputs: Build, test, package, and deploy-to-first-ring stages running green on a placeholder increment
Skeleton execution telemetry (build time, test results, deploy success, gate behaviour)
Handover pack for the CD Readiness Review

tasks.name: Define Branching Strategy
tasks.purpose: Select and document the target branching model and supporting policies — model (trunk-based / GitFlow / release-branch / hybrid), PR policies, required reviewers, build-validation rules, hotfix path and merge-back rules — grounded in the Branching & Release Strategy Context and aligned to the Pipeline Architecture. The Branching Strategy governs how every increment flows from commit to Release Candidate.

tasks.name: Define Pipeline Architecture
tasks.purpose: Design the end-to-end CI/CD pipeline architecture that every Delivery Loop will run on — stages, triggers, ring progression, gate integration points, artefact flow, version handling — grounded in the DevOps Toolchain Context and the Initial Solution Architecture. The Pipeline Architecture is the master blueprint: Branching Strategy, Quality Gates & Observability, Secrets & Config Management, and Initial Pipeline Skeleton all implement against it.
outputs: Reference pipeline implementation (as diagram or IaC outline)

tasks.name: Define Quality Gates & Observability
tasks.purpose: Define the catalogue of quality gates (automated and manual) and the observability plan (signals, thresholds, dashboards, alerting, DORA target bands) that the CD pipeline enforces across all rings and production. This is the control surface for the whole stream: Define Gate Criteria for Loop selects from it, Track DORA Metrics measures against it, Run Proactive Monitoring watches it, Production Monitoring & Alerting implements it.

tasks.name: Define Release & Ring Cadence
tasks.purpose: Set the target cadence for promoting increments through the ring model and the cadence for production deployments — including CAB / CCB touchpoints, change-freeze windows and rollback-and-replay windows — aligned to the Transformation Release Plan, the Branching Strategy and the Target Environment Topology. The cadence is the rhythm that Manage Release Windows & Cadence operates each loop and that Production Cutover follows at Deploy.

tasks.name: Define Rollback & DR Approach
tasks.purpose: Define the rollback strategy for each ring (including production) and the disaster-recovery approach needed to meet the RPO / RTO commitments captured in Operability Requirements. Rollback covers controlled, pipeline-driven reversal of a bad deploy; DR covers broader platform-failure recovery. Both are authored here and operated by Orchestrate Non-Prod Promotions, Production Cutover and Run Hypercare Support.
outputs: Rollback runbooks (at pointer level; detailed runbooks live with Pipeline Runbooks in Deploy)

tasks.name: Define Secrets & Config Management Approach
tasks.purpose: Define the approach for managing secrets (credentials, keys, tokens, certificates) and configuration (application, infrastructure, feature flags) across the ring model — sourcing, rotation, access, audit, integration with the pipeline. The approach is grounded in the Security Guardrails from the Security stream and the Target Environment Topology, and is operated loop-by-loop by Manage Config & Secrets Lifecycle.

tasks.name: Define Target Environment Topology
tasks.purpose: Design the target ring model that Delivery Loops will operate and Deploy will cut over to — rings (dev / test / UAT / staging / production / DR / ephemeral), their purpose, access model, data-refresh cadence, connectivity, shared vs dedicated resources — grounded in Environment Topology Context, Initial Solution Architecture and Operability Requirements. The topology is the physical contract behind the pipeline.
outputs: Target Environment Topology diagram and description

tasks.name: Refine CD Foundation from First Pipeline Run
tasks.purpose: Consolidate Initial Pipeline Skeleton execution telemetry and CD Readiness Review outputs into concrete, targeted adjustments to the Foundation artefacts — Pipeline Architecture, Branching Strategy, Target Environment Topology, Release & Ring Cadence, Quality Gates & Observability, Rollback & DR Approach, Secrets & Config Management — before the first Delivery Loop starts. This task closes the Foundation loop: design meets implementation, and implementation feeds back into design. Each wave runs this refinement once, then hands the improved Foundation to Delivery Loops.
outputs: Updated Foundation Artefacts (applied directly or routed to owners)
Foundation Refinement Log linking to the Readiness Review

tasks.name: Run CD Readiness Review
tasks.purpose: Run the Foundation-closing gate review that validates every Foundation artefact is ready for Delivery Loops to begin. The review walks the Pipeline Architecture, Branching Strategy, Target Environment Topology, Release & Ring Cadence, Quality Gates & Observability, Rollback & DR Approach, Secrets & Config Management and Initial Pipeline Skeleton against a readiness checklist, captures decisions and actions, and issues a CD Readiness Sign-off (go / conditional / no-go). Without this gate, Delivery Loops start on an ungoverned pipeline baseline.
outputs: CD Readiness Sign-off decision (go / conditional / no-go)
Actions register with owners and due dates

tasks.name: Create Data Strategy
tasks.purpose: Produce the engagement data strategy — the target data architecture, data domains, source systems, transformation approach, migration approach, quality bar, and ownership. The strategy is the control document for all Delivery Loops data tasks and the basis for the target data model and migration plan.
outputs: Target data architecture (store, model, integration pattern)
Data quality bar and data-ownership model
Data migration approach (waves, cutover strategy, reconciliation)
Key decisions cited from state/decisions/ (target architecture, migration approach, quality bar, ownership)

tasks.name: Build Adoption Plan
tasks.purpose: The Change Management Plan sets the *approach* to organisational change. The Adoption Plan turns that approach into the concrete interventions that make users ready: which user groups need what training, in what format, on what schedule, delivered by whom, with what materials, and measured how. It is the plan that ensures users are actually ready at go-live rather than merely informed that go-live is coming.
outputs: User-group profiles mapped to the delivery scope they are impacted by
Adoption success measures and targets per group, with leading indicators
The training delivery schedule, phased against the release and go-live milestones
Training materials and guides inventory, with author, reviewer, and readiness date per item
The enablement and support model through go-live and into hypercare
Adoption measurement and reporting cadence, and the escalation route for a shortfall

tasks.name: Build Change Management Plan
tasks.purpose: A solution that works and is never adopted delivers no value. The Change Management Plan is the engagement's approach to the *organisational* side of that risk: which parts of the customer's organisation this programme changes, how significant that change is for each group, how those groups are communicated with and brought along, and how organisational readiness is measured before go-live is ever considered.
outputs: The change vision and case for change, traced to the business outcomes
Impacted-group segmentation with the change approach per group
The escalation path for disputes, risks, issues, and blockers, on both customer and Microsoft sides
Organisational readiness measures and their checkpoints
Change roles and responsibilities, including the sponsor and change-champion structure

tasks.name: Generate Project Status Report
tasks.purpose: Produce a Project Status Report that gives the project manager, team leads, and stakeholders a clear picture of sprint-level progress, resource utilisation, financials, and risks. This is the operational status artefact that tracks day-to-day delivery health — it feeds the Program Status Report (for multi-project programs), the SteerCo Presentation, and sprint-level decision-making. It provides the timeline view against the Program Roadmap and aggregates key outcomes from all active streams.
outputs: Program / Project Performance & Business Value Tracking

tasks.name: Manage Change Requests
tasks.purpose: Maintain the Change Request & CCB Log — the living register that tracks every scope, schedule, budget, or quality change request from submission through impact assessment to CCB decision. This artefact is the formal record of what was proposed, why, what the impact would be, and what was decided. It feeds the CCB Meeting (decision queue), SteerCo Presentation (escalated changes), and Release Plan (approved scope adjustments). Azure DevOps is the system of record for tracking change request work items.

tasks.name: Manage Resources
tasks.purpose: Produce Resource & Staffing Updates — the periodic artefact that tracks team capacity, utilisation, ramp up/down execution, and skills coverage against the Resource / Staffing Plan throughout delivery. This artefact ensures the team is right-sized for each sprint and release, flags under/over-allocation early, and manages GRM requests, onboarding, and offboarding. It feeds the Project Status Report (resource utilisation section), Financials Updates (resource cost impact), and Sprint Planning (capacity input).

tasks.name: Monitor Partner Performance
tasks.purpose: Produce the Partner & Subcontractor Performance Report — the periodic artefact that monitors delivery quality, SLA adherence, collaboration health, and capacity of partner and subcontractor resources engaged on the project. This artefact ensures partners are delivering to the agreed standard, flags performance issues early, and provides the evidence base for contract reviews, resource adjustments, and escalations. It feeds the Project Status Report (partner performance section), SteerCo Presentation (partner escalations), and Resource & Staffing Updates (partner capacity).

tasks.name: Monitor Program Financials
tasks.purpose: Produce Financials Updates — the periodic financial health check that compares budget against actuals, updates the forecast, tracks ECIF and consumption spend, and flags variances that require action. This artefact keeps the financial baseline honest throughout delivery. It feeds the Program Status Report and Project Status Report (financial summary sections), SteerCo Presentation (budget narrative), and Change Request & CCB Log (cost impact of approved changes). ESXP is the system of record for actuals and forecasting.

tasks.name: Monitor RAID and Blockers
tasks.purpose: Maintain the RAID & Blocker Log — the living register of Risks, Actions, Issues, and Decisions plus sprint-level blockers that tracks threats and impediments throughout delivery. This artefact is consumed by virtually every governance forum (SteerCo, ARB, CCB) and feeds Sprint Planning (blocker-aware scope), Sprint Daily Updates (impediment escalation), and Program/Project Status Reports (risk posture). It is the single source of truth for what is threatening or blocking the engagement.

tasks.name: Prepare SteerCo Presentation
tasks.purpose: Prepare the Steering Committee (SteerCo) presentation — the executive-level briefing that drives governance decisions, approvals, and escalation resolution. The SteerCo Presentation distils the Program and Project Status Reports into an audience-appropriate deck for executive sponsors, customer leadership, and Microsoft delivery leadership. It highlights progress against business outcomes, surfaces decisions that require SteerCo authority (scope changes, budget adjustments, risk escalations), and provides the governance forum with the information needed to steer the engagement.

tasks.name: Produce Program Status Report
tasks.purpose: Produce a Program Status Report that provides the program director and executive sponsors with a consolidated view of progress, risks, finances, and outcomes across all projects and streams in the program. This is the governance-grade artefact that feeds the SteerCo Presentation and program-level decision-making. It aggregates key outcomes from all streams, tracks milestone progress against the Program Roadmap, and highlights cross-project dependencies and escalations.
outputs: Program / Project Performance & Business Value Tracking

tasks.name: Run ARB Meeting
tasks.purpose: Execute the Architecture Review Board (ARB) meeting — the technical governance forum that reviews solution architecture decisions, evaluates design changes, assesses technical risks, and approves or rejects architectural proposals. The ARB Summary captures architecture decisions, technical debt items, and design direction, feeding the Governance Rhythm Summary and downstream solution delivery.

tasks.name: Run CCB Meeting
tasks.purpose: Execute the Change Control Board (CCB) meeting — the governance forum that evaluates, approves, rejects, or defers change requests that affect scope, schedule, budget, or quality. The CCB Summary captures decisions on each change request, impact assessments, and any conditions attached to approvals. It feeds the Governance Rhythm Summary, updates the Change Request & CCB Log, and informs release planning and resource adjustments.

tasks.name: Run Governance Rhythm
tasks.purpose: Maintain the overall governance rhythm for the engagement — the recurring cadence of SteerCo, ARB, and CCB meetings that keeps decision-making, architecture oversight, and change control on track. This artefact is the master governance calendar and consolidated summary of all governance forum outcomes. It ensures meetings happen on schedule, decisions are recorded, and action items are tracked to closure. The individual forum summaries (SteerCo Summary, ARB Summary, CCB Summary) feed into this consolidated view.

tasks.name: Run Phase Gate Reviews
tasks.purpose: Execute formal go/no-go gate reviews at release and phase boundaries — validating that exit criteria are met, deliverables are accepted, test results are within tolerance, and the engagement is ready to proceed to the next phase or release. Release Sign-off & Quality-Gate Reviews are the formal checkpoints that prevent premature transitions and ensure quality thresholds are maintained. Gate findings feed into the RAID & Blocker Log, and gate decisions are recorded for audit trail and governance compliance.

tasks.name: Run Sprint Daily Updates
tasks.purpose: Track daily sprint progress, surface impediments early, and keep the team aligned on the Sprint Goal through structured daily standups and sprint board updates. Sprint Daily Updates is the continuous evaluation heartbeat within each sprint — it feeds impediment data into RAID Management, progress signals into Sprint Review, and burndown trends into Program Status reporting.

tasks.name: Run Sprint Planning
tasks.purpose: Produce the Sprint Plan for the upcoming sprint — a committed scope of work derived from the prioritised backlog, aligned to the Program Roadmap and Release Plan, and sized against available team capacity. Sprint Planning is the cadence heartbeat of Delivery Loops: it translates Foundation artefacts (roadmap, release plan, resource plan) into a concrete, time-boxed commitment that Solution, Continuous Delivery, Data, and Change streams execute against. The Sprint Plan feeds Sprint Daily (progress tracking), Sprint Review (demo scope), and Sprint Retro (retrospective baseline).

tasks.name: Run Sprint Retro
tasks.purpose: Reflect on the completed sprint to identify what went well, what didn't, and what to improve — then commit to concrete action items for the next sprint. Sprint Retro Results are the refinement mechanism that closes the Delivery Loop: lessons learned feed directly into the next Sprint Planning session, process improvements feed into governance adjustments, and recurring blockers escalate into RAID actions. This is the only Delivery Loops × Transformation row in refinement — it is the loop's learning engine.

tasks.name: Run Sprint Review
tasks.purpose: Demonstrate completed sprint work to stakeholders, validate that delivered increments meet acceptance criteria and align with the Sprint Goal, and gather feedback that shapes the next sprint's priorities. Sprint Review Results are the formal evaluation gate at the end of each sprint — they confirm what was accepted, what was rejected or deferred, and what new insights emerged. The results feed Sprint Retro (process improvement), Program Status Reports (progress tracking), and Sprint Planning (backlog re-prioritisation for the next loop).

tasks.name: Run SteerCo Meeting
tasks.purpose: Execute the Steering Committee meeting — the highest governance forum on the engagement where executive sponsors, customer leadership, and Microsoft delivery leadership make programme-level decisions, approve scope changes, resolve escalations, and confirm strategic alignment. The SteerCo Summary captures decisions made, action items assigned, and escalations resolved or deferred, feeding the Governance Rhythm Summary and downstream planning.

tasks.name: Run TQA and InfoSec Review
tasks.purpose: Execute periodic TQA and InfoSec reviews that assess whether solution and governance artefacts meet the agreed quality and security standards before release. This artefact combines technical quality assurance (TQA) with information security posture assessment — ensuring deliverables are architecturally sound, functionally complete, tested to the required level, and compliant with the ISRA baseline and Security Guardrails. Quality and security findings feed into the RAID & Blocker Log, and inform the ARB (architecture quality), SteerCo (quality and security posture reporting), and the Final InfoSec Sign-off at Deploy.

tasks.name: Build AI Backend Prototype
tasks.purpose: Build a working AI backend prototype — a demonstrable, end-to-end AI capability that validates the solution hypotheses against real or representative data. Unlike the Foundation Solution Prototype which proves platform processes, this prototype proves the AI components: model/prompt performance, agent behaviour, RAG retrieval quality, and integration with the business process layer. The prototype is used to gather stakeholder feedback, refine hypotheses, and de-risk the AI architecture before full-scale implementation. This task is relevant only for Pure Agentic and Hybrid archetypes.
outputs: AI backend components (model serving, prompt chains, RAG retrieval, agent logic)
Agent behaviour prototype with guardrails (Agentic archetypes)
Evaluation results (accuracy, latency, relevance, safety metrics)
Stakeholder feedback and hypothesis validation status (confirmed / partially confirmed / refuted)
Delivering Features advanced in state/backlog/ via rapid-toolkit-manage-state, recording the AI components built and their evaluation status
Unresolved actions and issues recorded in state/actions/ and state/issues/ via rapid-toolkit-manage-state

tasks.name: Build & Execute Migration Pipelines
tasks.purpose: Build repeatable data migration pipelines and execute incremental migration loads every Delivery Loop. Translates the Data Migration Strategy into working, automated pipelines that move data from source systems to the target environment — validating with business users each loop and tracking "migration confidence" as a trend metric. Co-runs with the Data stream's Execute Data Migration task: the Data stream owns the data-engineering execution (ETL performance, reconciliation, audit); the Solution stream owns pipeline design, business validation, and acceptance sign-off.
outputs: Working, automated migration pipelines for in-scope domains
Validated data loaded to target environment

tasks.name: Build Integration Components
tasks.purpose: Build the integration components that connect the target platform to external systems, data sources, and services. Each integration is designed per the Integration Architecture Blueprint, implemented as APIs, connectors, middleware flows, or event-driven pipelines, and tested against the receiving/sending systems. The output is a set of working, tested integration artefacts ready for assembly into the Working Solution.
outputs: Working, tested integration components connecting the target platform to external systems
Documented specifications ready for assembly into Working Solutions

tasks.name: Build Reports & Dashboards
tasks.purpose: Build the business reports, dashboards, and analytics artefacts defined in the Reporting & Analytics Strategy — Power BI reports, D365 dashboards, embedded analytics, AI insight dashboards, and self-service workspaces. Reports are built iteratively alongside the solution — as each E2E process goes live, its operational reports are built in the same loop. Reports are demonstrated in Sprint Demos for business feedback.
outputs: Power BI reports, D365 dashboards, AI insight dashboards, and self-service workspaces built for this loop's in-scope processes

tasks.name: Build Solution Configuration
tasks.purpose: Produce the platform configuration artefacts — parameter settings, security roles, workflow rules, business rules, entity customisations, and environment-specific settings — that define how the target platform behaves for this engagement. Configuration is driven by the SDD and Fit/Gap Register: standard capabilities are configured per the design, and gap resolutions that require configuration (as opposed to code) are applied here. The output is a documented, reproducible configuration set that can be promoted across environments.
outputs: A documented, reproducible platform configuration set covering security, business rules, entity customisations, and environment parameters

tasks.name: Build UX/UI Design
tasks.purpose: Design and build the user experience and interface layer of the solution — custom screens, dashboards, portals, conversational interfaces, and agent interaction surfaces. UX/UI design translates requirements and process flows into interfaces that end users interact with daily. For Agentic/Hybrid archetypes, this includes conversational UX, agent feedback surfaces, and human-in-the-loop interaction patterns.
outputs: Custom screens, dashboards, portals, and conversational interfaces implemented on the target platform
Aligned with user journeys and accessibility standards

tasks.name: Build Working Solutions
tasks.purpose: Assemble the complete working solution increment for each sprint — integrating configured processes, extensions, integrations, data migrations, and AI components into a cohesive, deployable build. Where Implement E2E Processes focuses on individual process chains, this task ensures the full solution hangs together: cross-process dependencies resolved, integration points connected, data flowing correctly, and the build passing baseline quality gates before it enters evaluation.
outputs: A validated, deployable solution increment integrating all sprint deliverables (processes, configuration, integrations, AI components)
A cohesive build ready for evaluation
Delivering Features and their user stories advanced in state/backlog/ via rapid-toolkit-manage-state, recording the increment's components and build reference
Build-level defects recorded in state/issues/ and the build validation sign-off in state/decisions/ via rapid-toolkit-manage-state

tasks.name: Finalise Cutover Strategy
tasks.purpose: Refine and finalise the Cutover Strategy based on Delivery Loop learnings — detailing the cutover runbook with specific timings, owners, and dependencies; incorporating migration pipeline maturity and test results; updating the ACM plan with actual training completion and communications readiness; and producing the detailed, rehearsal-ready cutover plan that Deploy will execute.

tasks.name: Implement E2E Processes
tasks.purpose: Implement end-to-end business processes on the target platform, turning the Reference Process Model into working, demonstrable process flows that span functional boundaries. Each sprint takes a slice of the process model and configures, extends, or builds it until the process runs E2E in the development environment. The result is the backbone of the solution — tested process chains that the customer can see, walk through, and accept.
outputs: Working end-to-end business process flows running in the development environment, demonstrable to stakeholders
Test evidence recorded and defects logged

tasks.name: Manage Defect Triage
tasks.purpose: Manage the defect triage process — a structured, recurring ceremony where the delivery team and customer prioritise, categorise, and disposition defects found during all testing gates (Process Testing, E2E/SIT, Performance, UAT, Usability, AI Back-Testing). Defect triage ensures that critical defects are resolved before they block downstream activities, that defects are correctly categorised (fix now, defer, out-of-scope, by-design), and that the defect backlog remains actionable.
outputs: A maintained, categorised defect backlog in ADO with triage decisions recorded

tasks.name: Monitor AI Solution Quality
tasks.purpose: Establish and operate continuous monitoring and observability for all AI and agentic components in the solution — tracking output quality, grounding accuracy, responsible AI compliance, performance against SLAs, and data/concept drift. Generative AI models are inherently non-deterministic and probabilistic; their outputs can vary for similar inputs and degrade over time as data and context shift. This task ensures the delivery team detects quality degradation, guardrail violations, and performance issues early — within each Delivery Loop — rather than discovering them post-deployment. It is a recurring eval capability that runs from the first loop where AI components are active through Deploy and into production operations.
outputs: Quality monitoring dashboard (grounding accuracy, response quality, guardrail compliance)
Performance monitoring dashboard (latency, throughput, token usage, availability)
Responsible AI monitoring (toxicity, bias, PII detection)
Active from the first Delivery Loop with AI components through Deploy and production operations

tasks.name: Prepare AI Context & Data
tasks.purpose: Prepare the AI context and data that feed agent and AI-driven solution components — data quality validation, RAG context preparation (document chunking, embedding configuration, knowledge source mapping), grounding data availability, and context window optimisation. For agentic solutions this ensures agents have high-quality, well-structured, discoverable knowledge to reason over. This task is relevant only for Pure Agentic and Hybrid archetypes.
outputs: Validated knowledge index with chunking and embedding configuration

tasks.name: Produce Documentation (FDDs, TDDs)
tasks.purpose: Produce Functional Design Documents (FDDs) and Technical Design Documents (TDDs) that record how the solution was built — the design decisions, configuration choices, extension specifications, integration contracts, and data models behind each Working Solution increment. These documents serve as the knowledge transfer vehicle for operations handover, future maintenance, and audit trails. They are living documents updated each sprint as the solution evolves.
outputs: A set of Functional Design Documents and Technical Design Documents covering all solution components built in the sprint
Traceable to the SDD and Fit/Gap Register

tasks.name: Refine Solution Design Document
tasks.purpose: Iteratively update the Solution Design Document (SDD) at the end of each Delivery Loop to incorporate sprint demo feedback, ARB/CCB decisions, and test results into the design baseline. The SDD is a living document — v1.0 is baselined in Foundation, and each Delivery Loop refines it as the team validates design assumptions against working solution behaviour, discovers integration issues through testing, and resolves change requests through the ARB/CCB governance process. This task ensures the SDD always reflects the current approved design state, maintaining a single source of truth for the solution design that Build, Test, and Deploy activities reference. Refinement is incremental — only affected sections are updated, preserving the stability of validated design areas.
outputs: Full version history with traceability to decision sources
Published to the project repository as the new design baseline for the next Delivery Loop

tasks.name: Run AI Back-Testing
tasks.purpose: Run back-testing against the AI backend — evaluating model/prompt/agent performance on historical or held-out data to validate that the solution hypotheses hold under realistic conditions. Back-testing provides the quantitative evidence for hypothesis confirmation or refutation, and feeds directly into the Refine Solution Hypotheses refinement step. This task is relevant only for Pure Agentic and Hybrid archetypes.
outputs: Hypothesis validation status (confirmed / partially confirmed / refuted)

tasks.name: Run E2E/SIT Testing
tasks.purpose: Execute end-to-end and system integration test (SIT) scripts — verifying that business processes work correctly across module boundaries, integrations, and data flows. Where Process Testing validates individual processes in isolation, E2E/SIT testing validates the solution as an integrated whole. Test execution follows logical business process groups to simulate real-world usage patterns.
outputs: Pass/fail rates per business process group and integration point

tasks.name: Run Performance Testing
tasks.purpose: Execute performance and benchmarking tests — validating that the Working Solutions meet the non-functional requirements (NFRs) for response time, throughput, concurrent users, and resource utilisation. Performance testing identifies bottlenecks before production deployment and provides the evidence base for capacity planning and infrastructure sizing.

tasks.name: Run Process Testing
tasks.purpose: Execute process test scripts against the Working Solutions — verifying that each configured business process behaves correctly in isolation. Process testing validates individual process chains (happy path + exception paths) before they enter broader E2E/SIT testing. Defects found here are logged, triaged, and fed back to the development team for resolution within the sprint or the next sprint.
outputs: Coverage metrics against the Test Strategy

tasks.name: Run Solution ARB/CCB Reviews
tasks.purpose: Run the Architecture Review Board (ARB) and Change Control Board (CCB) as recurring governance ceremonies during Delivery Loops to evaluate solution design changes, validate architectural integrity, approve or reject change requests, and ensure the evolving solution remains aligned with the Initial Solution Architecture and the SDD. The ARB governs technical fitness — architecture decisions, extension/customisation approaches, integration patterns, and non-functional compliance. The CCB governs scope fitness — change requests, gap-resolution dispositions, backlog reprioritisation, and release scope adjustments. Together they ensure that every design change is deliberate, traceable, and aligned with business outcomes before it is implemented. This is a continuous eval capability — reviews run every loop, not as a one-off gate.
outputs: ARB decision log (architectural decisions with rationale)
CCB decision log (scope/change decisions with rationale)
Review outcome summary communicated to the delivery team

tasks.name: Run Sprint Demo
tasks.purpose: Run the Sprint Demo — a time-boxed showcase of the sprint's Working Solutions to the wider project stakeholders (customer project team, SteerCo representatives, business owners). The demo validates that the solution meets acceptance criteria, surfaces misalignments early, and captures feedback that feeds back into the next sprint's planning. Every sprint must end with a demo — it is the primary transparency mechanism in Delivery Loops.
outputs: A recorded demonstration of the sprint's Working Solutions to stakeholders

tasks.name: Run Usability & Accessibility Testing
tasks.purpose: Run usability and accessibility testing — evaluating how effectively end users can interact with the solution's UX/UI, conversational interfaces, and agent surfaces, and verifying that the solution meets accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA minimum). Usability testing identifies friction points, confusing workflows, and interaction barriers. Accessibility testing ensures the solution is perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust for users with disabilities — including screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation, colour contrast, focus management, and assistive technology support. For Agentic/Hybrid archetypes, this also validates conversational UX, agent feedback clarity, and human-in-the-loop interaction patterns.
outputs: Screen reader and keyboard navigation results
Prioritised improvement recommendations logged in ADO

tasks.name: Define Gate Criteria for Loop
tasks.purpose: Establish the loop-specific quality and governance gates applied to this Delivery Loop's increment — which automated gates must pass (SIT, security scan, code-quality thresholds), which manual gates are required (ARB, CCB, UAT sign-off), and what constitutes a rollback trigger. The output grounds Non-Prod Ring Promotions, Release Candidate production, and Release Windows & Cadence in explicit, loop-scoped criteria rather than relying on implicit Foundation defaults.
outputs: Automated gates with explicit numeric thresholds (SIT pass rate, security scan, code-quality gate, dependency scan)
Manual gates with named approvers by role (ARB, CCB, UAT sign-off)

tasks.name: Detect Environment Drift
tasks.purpose: Continuously compare the actual state of every non-prod and production environment against the Target Environment Topology and declared Infrastructure-as-Code baseline. Drift that goes undetected makes promotions unreliable, pipelines flaky, and incidents hard to root-cause. This task classifies every drift item (authorised change / unauthorised / legacy / dependency) and routes findings into Refine Environment Health and, where remediation is automated, back into the pipeline.
outputs: Refinement input feed for Refine Environment Health

tasks.name: Ensure Stable Solution
tasks.purpose: Maintain a stable, releasable solution across every environment throughout the loop. Detect regressions fast, stabilise the trunk, and keep the solution in a state where it can be promoted on demand — the continuous-delivery foundation for every outcome.
outputs: Regression ticket summary with triage status
SIT pass/fail summary within the agreed SLA

tasks.name: Execute Continuous System Integration Testing (SIT)
tasks.purpose: Run continuous system integration testing across the end-to-end flows defined in the CD reference business model. SIT is the gate that confirms the loop's increments integrate correctly with the rest of the solution — not just unit-correct, but end-to-end correct.
outputs: Pass / fail status per end-to-end flow
Raised defect, data, and environment tickets

tasks.name: Ingest Increment for Promotion
tasks.purpose: Ingest each Delivery Loop's working-solution increment — build artefact(s), test results, integration build — and stage it as the pipeline's input for promotion through non-prod rings. The task turns "something the Solution stream shipped" into a versioned, attested, metadata-tagged increment the CD pipeline can run gate checks against, promote, and package into a Release Candidate. Feeds Non-Prod Ring Promotions, Release Candidate, and the Loop's Gate Criteria.
outputs: Staged increment ready for ring promotion
Increment manifest (version, components, test status, provenance)
Notification to gate owners that the increment is ready for evaluation

tasks.name: Manage Config & Secrets Lifecycle
tasks.purpose: Operate the Secrets & Config Management Approach loop by loop — create, rotate, retire secrets and configuration entries across rings, enforce access controls, audit access and propagate changes safely through the pipeline. Keeps the Foundation-defined approach living and current rather than a static document. Feeds Detect Environment Drift and Refine Pipeline & Automation.
outputs: Provisioned / rotated / retired secrets and config entries

tasks.name: Manage Pipelines
tasks.purpose: Own the CI/CD pipelines — build, test, release — across environments and release trains. Keep pipelines fast, reliable, and aligned to the engagement's delivery cadence. Evolve pipelines per loop as the solution grows.
outputs: Build, test, and release pipeline definitions aligned to release trains
Pipeline performance metrics (build time, test time, release time)

tasks.name: Manage Release Windows & Cadence
tasks.purpose: Operate the Release & Ring Cadence plan loop by loop — schedule release windows, coordinate with Transformation governance (CAB / CCB), manage change-freeze windows, handle exception requests — so non-prod promotions and Release Candidate production happen in rhythm with the agreed cadence. Drift from cadence is a signal that feeds Refine Pipeline & Automation.
outputs: CAB / CCB agendas and decision records (for CD-owned changes)

tasks.name: Manage Test Data
tasks.purpose: Operate the test-data lifecycle across non-prod rings so every SIT, UAT and performance run executes against representative, compliant data sets — refresh from approved sources, masking / anonymisation, seeding, versioning, remediation. Coordinates with the Data stream for transformation logic; the CD stream owns the pipeline and ring-level mechanics of getting test data into the right place at the right time.
outputs: Masked, versioned test-data sets loaded per ring
Test-Data Catalogue with versions and provenance

tasks.name: Orchestrate Non-Prod Promotions
tasks.purpose: Operate the pipeline each loop to promote the staged increment through the non-prod rings — dev → test → UAT → staging — as each ring's gate set passes. Non-prod promotions produce the fully-validated increment that Produce Release Candidate attests and publishes. This is the CD stream's day-to-day work inside a Delivery Loop.
outputs: Promoted increments through each non-prod ring
Promotion audit trail (which rings, which gates, when, duration)
Halt notifications routed to owners on gate failure

tasks.name: Produce Release Candidate
tasks.purpose: Produce a signed, tested, attested **Release Candidate** artefact from the staged increment once every non-prod ring has passed its gates. The Release Candidate is the CD stream's primary deliverable output of each Delivery Loop — it's what Deploy phase cuts over to production. The attestation bundle (SIT results, SAST / SCA reports, build provenance, test evidence) is the contract that makes production deployment auditable and rollback traceable.
inputs: SIT Results, SAST / SCA Reports, Test Evidence
outputs: Metadata manifest (version, components, source commit, pipeline run, gate evidence)
Delivering Features advanced in state/backlog/ via rapid-toolkit-manage-state, recording the RC version, source commit, and build-run ID
RC gate decision recorded in state/decisions/ via rapid-toolkit-manage-state, citing the attestation bundle by store location and signature

tasks.name: Refine Environment Health
tasks.purpose: Consolidate the Delivery Loop's environment-health evidence — Detect Environment Drift eval output and production-adjacent telemetry — into concrete adjustments to the Target Environment Topology, Run Infrastructure, Secrets & Config Management Approach and Rollback & DR. This refinement task keeps the ring model from eroding loop by loop: drift gets classified, patterns get caught, and the environment baseline gets updated rather than silently diverging.
outputs: Routed change requests to owning rows

tasks.name: Refine Pipeline & Automation
tasks.purpose: Consolidate the Delivery Loop's eval-group signals — DORA Metrics, Proactive Monitoring, SIT results, Defect triage — into concrete, prioritised adjustments to the CD pipeline, automation coverage, quality gates and branching rules. This task closes the loop: evidence becomes change proposals that feed back into Manage Pipelines, Quality Gates & Observability and Branching Strategy for implementation in the next loop. Without this refinement, eval data just accumulates rather than improving the system.
inputs: Pipeline Architecture, Quality Gates & Observability, Branching Strategy
outputs: Routed change requests to Manage Pipelines, Quality Gates & Observability, Branching Strategy

tasks.name: Run Infrastructure
tasks.purpose: Operate the cloud infrastructure that backs the solution — environments, networks, identity, storage, compute — in every region required by the country scope. Keep it compliant, observable, and cost-controlled.
outputs: Provisioned environments matching the design and policy
Network, identity, and access policy enforcement status
Availability, performance, and cost telemetry and alerting
Cost-optimisation and right-sizing adjustments per loop

tasks.name: Run Proactive Monitoring
tasks.purpose: Actively monitor pipeline and platform signals — builds, deployments, environments, test runs, incidents and change tickets — to surface anomalies early and feed context into every Delivery Loop's decisions. Proactive monitoring replaces a passive "ingest telemetry once a week" posture with a daily-triage discipline: anomalies become flags that the loop must resolve before the next promotion, not problems discovered after they've shipped. Feeds DORA Metrics, Environment Drift eval, Pipeline & Automation adjustments refinement, and the Loop's Gate Criteria.

tasks.name: Track DORA Metrics
tasks.purpose: Continuously measure the four core DORA metrics (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, Mean Time to Restore) plus the fifth Reliability metric, against the target bands set in Foundation *Quality Gates & Observability*. The task produces the engineering-internal pipeline-health snapshot that drives Refine Pipeline & Automation each loop, and contributes to Reliability reporting during Deploy hypercare. DORA here is a measurement discipline, not a publication target — the scorecard informs engineering, not customer contracts.
inputs: Target Bands from Quality Gates & Observability
outputs: Flagged items for Refine Pipeline & Automation

tasks.name: Execute Data Migration
tasks.purpose: Execute the Data-stream view of migration — the specialist run that moves transformed data into the target environment on the loop's schedule. Co-runs with the Solution-stream *Build & Execute Migration Pipelines* task, contributing the data-engineering specialisation (performance, reconciliation, audit).
outputs: Rehearsal outcome and any corrective actions taken before the live run
Migrated data across the in-scope slices for this loop
Reconciliation report evidencing completeness and accuracy against the source extracts
Data-stream run report recording the migration window, volumes, and residual gaps

tasks.name: Execute Data Transformation
tasks.purpose: Execute the data transformation required for the loop — mapping, cleansing, enrichment, format conversion — so that downstream migration and integration can land data correctly into the target systems or agents.
outputs: Mapped, cleansed, and enriched data across in-scope slices
Data-quality check results and quarantine records
Sign-off record from the customer data owner

tasks.name: Define Security Guardrails
tasks.purpose: Define and record the agreed security controls — identity, access, data protection, and AI guardrails — applied to the loop's working-solution increments. Ensures that each loop's outcome ships with guardrails in place, not bolted on later, and that the applied controls are written down as reviewable evidence for the loop gate and for the Deploy-phase InfoSec sign-off.
outputs: Threat model delta for the loop's increments, citing .project/context/security/
AI guardrails applied (content safety, grounding, eval gates) for agentic components
Security validation results (scans, policy checks, penetration smoke)
Findings disposition and loop sign-off, citing the state/risks/ and state/decisions/ IDs

tasks.name: Assess Go-Live Readiness
tasks.purpose: Produce the Go-Live Readiness & Go/No-Go Checklist — the formal assessment that validates all workstreams are ready for production cutover and the customer has accepted the solution. This artefact consolidates readiness evidence from every stream (solution quality, test results, operations preparedness, security compliance, data migration completeness, CD pipeline readiness) into a structured checklist with a binary go/no-go decision. It is the final gate before production cutover begins.

tasks.name: Capture Lessons Learned
tasks.purpose: Produce the Lessons Learned artefact — a structured capture of engagement insights covering what went well, what didn't, and actionable recommendations for future engagements. This draws from the cumulative retrospective data in Azure DevOps and synthesises it into a categorised, reusable record. The Lessons Learned artefact feeds the Project Closeout Report and the Knowledge Garden for organisational learning.

tasks.name: Close Program Financials
tasks.purpose: Produce the Final Financial Close-out — the definitive financial reconciliation that closes the engagement's budget, reconciles all actuals against the original baseline, finalises ECIF and consumption spend, resolves outstanding financial items, and produces the audit-grade financial record. This artefact feeds the Project Closeout Report and is the financial evidence for customer sign-off and internal audit.

tasks.name: Complete Final Security Assessment
tasks.purpose: Complete the Final InfoSec Sign-off — the production-readiness security gate that validates the code repository against security standards, confirms all vulnerabilities identified during delivery are remediated, and obtains formal InfoSec approval before go-live. This is the definitive security clearance for the production deployment, distinct from the periodic TQA and InfoSec reviews during Delivery Loops. It feeds the Go-Live Readiness & Go/No-Go Checklist as security evidence.

tasks.name: Confirm Operations Readiness
tasks.purpose: Produce the Operations Readiness Plan — the formal validation that the customer's operations team, support processes, monitoring, escalation paths, and runbooks are in place to own and operate the solution post-go-live. This artefact is a prerequisite for the Go-Live Readiness & Go/No-Go Checklist and ensures that go-live does not occur before the customer can sustain the solution independently. It covers people (trained support staff), process (incident management, escalation, SLA monitoring), and tooling (monitoring dashboards, alerting, runbooks).

tasks.name: Execute Support Handover
tasks.purpose: Execute the formal handover of solution ownership from the Microsoft delivery team to the customer's support and operations team. This artefact confirms that the support model is agreed, SLAs are defined, escalation paths are documented, knowledge transfer is complete, and the customer's team is ready to own and operate the solution independently. The Support Transition / Hand-off Confirmation is the formal record that the handover is complete — it closes the delivery team's operational responsibility.

tasks.name: Offboard Project Team
tasks.purpose: Produce the Team Offboarding Plan and execute the formal offboarding of all project team members — Microsoft, customer, and partner resources. This artefact ensures every team member is properly released from the engagement with access revoked, GRM requests closed, knowledge transfer completed, and offboarding checklists signed off. It is one of the final Deploy artefacts, executed after the Support Transition / Hand-off is confirmed and the delivery team's operational responsibility has ended.

tasks.name: Prepare and Execute Cutover Plan
tasks.purpose: Prepare and execute the Cutover Plan — the sequenced, time-boxed plan that orchestrates every activity required to switch from the current to the target solution in production. This covers data migration execution, configuration deployment, infrastructure provisioning, long-running process scheduling, Plan-B and roll-back scenarios, and post-cutover validation. The Cutover Execution Log tracks each step's status, timing, owner, and outcome in real time during the cutover window.

tasks.name: Prepare UAT Plan
tasks.purpose: Produce the UAT Plan — the structured plan that bridges the Foundation Test Strategies (governance and technical) into an executable User Acceptance Testing programme for the Deploy phase. This artefact defines who tests, what they test, with what data, in which environment, against which acceptance criteria, and on what schedule. It ensures customer business users are identified, available, trained on the test process, and equipped with scripts and data before UAT execution begins. The UAT Plan feeds directly into the Extended UAT execution (Solution stream) and the Go-Live Readiness & Go/No-Go Checklist.

tasks.name: Produce Closure Report
tasks.purpose: Produce the Project Closeout Report — the formal engagement closure document that summarises what was delivered against the original SOW, financial close-out status, lessons learned, outstanding items handed over, business value realised, and recommendations for future phases or BAU operations. This is the definitive record of the engagement and the last governance artefact produced. It is presented to the customer sponsor for formal acceptance and archived as the engagement's permanent record.

tasks.name: Publish Operations Guide
tasks.purpose: Publish the System Operations Guide — the technical operations manual that the customer's support and operations team uses for day-to-day solution management post-go-live. This artefact covers solution architecture overview, component inventory, configuration reference, monitoring and alerting setup, troubleshooting procedures, maintenance schedules, and known issues. It is the primary reference for L2/L3 support and feeds directly into the Operations Readiness Plan and Support Transition / Hand-off.

tasks.name: Report Final Program Status
tasks.purpose: Produce the Final Program / Project Status Report — the governance close-out record that consolidates delivery outcomes, financial actuals, lessons learned, RAID resolution status, and handover completeness into a single final report. This is the last status artefact of the engagement and the formal record of what was delivered, how it compared to the baseline, and what remains open. It feeds the Project Closeout Report and provides the evidence base for assessing realised value against the business outcomes in the context (`.project/context/value/`).

tasks.name: Build Production Release
tasks.purpose: Build the production release package — a validated, versioned, deployable artefact that bundles all solution components (application code, configuration, data migration scripts, integration configurations, AI pipeline artefacts) into a single release ready for production deployment. The production build is the final quality gate before cutover — it must pass all pre-deployment checks and be reproducible.
outputs: A versioned, validated production release package that has passed all pre-deployment checks and staging validation

tasks.name: Deliver Solution Walk-through
tasks.purpose: Deliver a structured solution walk-through (knowledge transfer) to the customer's operations, support, and business teams — a comprehensive tour of the delivered solution covering architecture, key processes, configuration decisions, integration points, and operational procedures. The walk-through complements the System Operations Guide and FDDs/TDDs with live, interactive demonstration and Q&A. It is the final knowledge transfer activity before the delivery team disengages.
outputs: Structured knowledge transfer sessions covering architecture, processes, AI components, and operations

tasks.name: Deploy to Production
tasks.purpose: Deploy the production release to the live production environment — executing the deployment runbook, verifying the deployment, and confirming that all components are operational. Deployment is distinct from cutover: deployment puts the software in place; cutover switches business operations to it. Deployment may happen before cutover (pre-staged) or as part of the cutover window.
outputs: All solution components deployed to the production environment

tasks.name: Execute Cutover Migration
tasks.purpose: Execute the cutover migration — the coordinated sequence of data migration, system switchover, and go-live activities that transitions the customer from their legacy systems to the new production environment. Cutover is rehearsed, time-boxed, and follows a detailed runbook. Success means production is live with migrated data, validated, and ready for business operations.
outputs: Production environment live with migrated data

tasks.name: Execute Cutover Plan
tasks.purpose: Execute the full cutover plan — orchestrating the end-to-end go-live sequence across all streams and dimensions: environment readiness, data migration (delegated to Execute Cutover Migration), integration switchover, ACM activation, security and access provisioning, AI/agent activation, communications, go/no-go gates, and hypercare activation. This is the master orchestration task — it coordinates all other Deploy tasks into a single timed, rehearsed execution.
outputs: Production environment live with all streams activated (solution, data, integrations, security, AI, ACM)

tasks.name: Hand Over to Operations
tasks.purpose: Formally transfer ownership of the production solution from the delivery team to the customer's operations team. Handover includes the System Operations Guide, runbooks, escalation procedures, monitoring dashboards, and knowledge transfer sessions. After handover, the operations team is self-sufficient for day-to-day support, and the delivery team transitions to advisory/hypercare only.
outputs: Formal transfer of production support ownership to the customer's operations team
System Operations Guide, runbooks, and monitoring dashboards delivered
Knowledge transfer delivered and signed off

tasks.name: Monitor Production AI Pipeline
tasks.purpose: Monitor AI components in production — tracking model performance, RAG retrieval quality, agent behaviour, safety guardrail compliance, drift detection, and cost metrics. Production AI monitoring is an ongoing capability, not a one-time check — it runs continuously during hypercare and is handed over to operations for long-term monitoring. This task is relevant only for Pure Agentic and Hybrid archetypes.
outputs: Continuous production AI monitoring with dashboards, drift detection, and guardrail compliance tracking

tasks.name: Publish Knowledge Garden
tasks.purpose: The Knowledge Garden is the engagement's single searchable body of context — aggregating all Foundation outputs (scope, requirements, reference processes, capability catalogue, legal/country constraints, team context, stakeholder maps) into a structured, AI-queryable repository. It is the context layer that every Delivery Loop task consumes. Publishing the Knowledge Garden means making all Foundation context discoverable, linked, and grounded — not just dumped into a folder.
outputs: A structured, indexed, cross-linked collection of all Foundation context artefacts in the project repository
Master index page and AI-agent discoverability via the discover-drive-kg skill

tasks.name: Refine Context
tasks.purpose: Close the RAPID loop by feeding production learnings, hypercare insights, and post-go-live feedback back into the context layer. Capture lessons learned, update the Knowledge Garden, refine the Reference Process Model based on actual usage, and document what worked and what didn't for future engagements. This is the final refinement step — it ensures the methodology's context layer reflects reality, not just design intent.

tasks.name: Rehearse Cutover
tasks.purpose: Execute mock cutovers — full or partial rehearsals of the cutover plan in a pre-production environment to validate timing, sequence, rollback procedures, and team readiness before the real go-live. Rehearsals surface gaps, timing miscalculations, and coordination failures while there is still time to fix them. At least 1–2 rehearsals must be completed before Execute Cutover Plan.
outputs: Updated cutover plan reflecting all findings
Cutover readiness assessment (ready / not ready / conditionally ready)

tasks.name: Release AI Pipeline
tasks.purpose: Release AI components to production — deploying prompt configurations, RAG indexes, agent orchestration, and monitoring to the live environment. The AI release is coordinated with the broader production deployment but has its own validation and rollback procedures due to the non-deterministic nature of AI components. This task is relevant only for Pure Agentic and Hybrid archetypes.
outputs: AI components deployed to production with model endpoints, RAG infrastructure, and agent orchestration

tasks.name: Run Extended UAT
tasks.purpose: Run extended User Acceptance Testing in the production environment after go-live — validating the solution under real business conditions with real data and real transaction volumes. Extended UAT catches issues that only surface in production (data edge cases, integration timing, load patterns) and confirms that the cutover was successful. It runs during the hypercare window alongside normal business operations.
outputs: Production-validated acceptance test results with formal sign-off

tasks.name: Run Smoke Testing
tasks.purpose: Run smoke tests immediately after production deployment and cutover — a fast, focused verification that core business processes work in the live environment. Smoke testing is the first quality gate after go-live: it catches deployment failures, configuration mismatches, and integration breaks before business users start working. If smoke tests fail, the rollback decision is triggered.
outputs: A pass/fail summary of critical process and integration health checks in the production environment

tasks.name: Run User Acceptance Testing
tasks.purpose: Execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) — the final validation gate where customer business users verify that the Working Solutions meet their requirements and are fit for purpose. UAT is conducted by the customer's own staff (not the delivery team) using business-representative scenarios and data. Acceptance sign-off from UAT is a prerequisite for production deployment.
outputs: Customer-executed acceptance test results with formal sign-off (full or conditional)
Defect log triaged by business impact

tasks.name: Understand Change of Requirements
tasks.purpose: Capture and classify change requests that emerge during hypercare and early production — new requirements, scope adjustments, and defects that surface under real business conditions. These changes feed back into the context layer, informing whether the solution needs another Delivery Loop iteration, a hotfix, or a backlog item for a future release. This is the Deploy-phase counterpart of the Foundation context tasks — it closes the RAPID loop by returning production learnings to context.
outputs: A classified, prioritised change request register with impact assessments
Loop-back decisions recorded for changes requiring further development

tasks.name: Validate Production Configuration
tasks.purpose: Validate that the production environment's configuration matches the intended design — security roles, business rules, integration endpoints, environment parameters, and feature flags are all set correctly for production.
