Configuration validation catches drift between what was designed (SDD) and what was deployed, preventing silent failures that smoke tests may not catch.
outputs: A validated production configuration with all settings confirmed against SDD

tasks.name: Validate Production Reporting
tasks.purpose: Validate reports and dashboards against production data — verifying that KPI calculations are correct with real volumes, refresh schedules work at production scale, row-level security filters correctly, and business stakeholders sign off on the analytics layer. Reports validated against test data during Delivery Loops may behave differently with production data volumes, data quality, and refresh timing.

tasks.name: Capture Hypercare Learnings
tasks.purpose: Consolidate the hypercare window's evidence — hypercare log, defect triage patterns, production telemetry, SLO / SLA breach record, support-optimisation tuning log, user feedback — into a structured Hypercare Learnings pack. The pack refines the CD Foundation (Pipeline Architecture, Quality Gates & Observability, Rollback & DR, Operability Requirements, Secrets & Config, Branching Strategy) and seeds the next wave's Delivery Loops. This is the single most valuable artefact produced during Deploy for cross-wave continuity.
inputs: SLO / SLA Adherence Scorecard & Breach Record
outputs: Categorised findings by owning Foundation artefact (Pipeline Architecture, Quality Gates & Observability, Rollback & DR, Operability Requirements, Secrets & Config, Branching Strategy)
Recommendations per owning artefact with expected impact and named owner
Consolidated evidence appendix (scorecard snapshots, tuning logs)
Lessons-learned contribution for the Transformation stream

tasks.name: Capture Production Telemetry
tasks.purpose: Aggregate post-go-live production signals — APM telemetry, SLO / SLA reports, production incidents, change tickets, and user feedback — during the Deploy-phase hypercare window. The output is the canonical context feed for Hypercare Support, Validate Production Quality, Measure SLO/SLA Adherence, Track Production Defect Resolution and Hypercare Learnings. Without a single aggregated snapshot, hypercare decisions fragment across tools.
inputs: Hypercare support channels and user feedback
outputs: Aggregated APM telemetry per service (latency, error rate, throughput, saturation)
SLO / SLA adherence data against the Operability Requirements targets
Incident and change-ticket register with severity, source, and release linkage
User-feedback register tagged by sentiment and severity

tasks.name: Execute Production Cutover
tasks.purpose: Execute the **technical production cutover** — run the CD pipeline against the Release Candidate following the Transformation Cutover Plan, coordinate with CCB / customer operations, perform pre- and post-cutover validation, and confirm success or trigger rollback. CD owns the **how** of cutover; Transformation owns the **when/whether** (Cutover Plan, Go-Live Sign-off). After cutover succeeds, Ship Release to Production produces the live Release artefact and Hypercare Support begins.
outputs: Cutover execution log (pipeline runs, timing, decisions)

tasks.name: Identify Post-Release Defects
tasks.purpose: Systematically identify, log, reproduce and root-cause post-release defects surfaced after production go-live — bugs, usability issues, performance regressions, integration failures, data issues. Link each defect back to the release and pipeline run that shipped it, so downstream Production Defect Resolution, Hypercare Learnings and CD Foundation refinement can act on real evidence rather than anecdotes. Complements Capture Production Telemetry by narrowing from "all signals" to "confirmed defects".

tasks.name: Measure SLO/SLA Adherence
tasks.purpose: Measure actual production performance against the SLO and SLA targets captured in Operability Requirements. This task owns the Reliability dimension of DORA during Deploy hypercare, provides the scorecard reported to Transformation (program performance) and, where breaches occur, roots them in root cause for Hypercare Learnings and Refine CD Foundation. Without this measurement, SLO / SLA commitments are aspirational rather than governed.
outputs: Reliability contribution to Track DORA Metrics

tasks.name: Operate Production Monitoring & Alerting
tasks.purpose: Operate the production observability stack during the hypercare window — monitors, dashboards, alerts, incident routing — against the thresholds defined in Quality Gates & Observability and the SLO / SLA targets in Operability Requirements. Provides the live signal that Capture Production Telemetry aggregates, the alert stream that Hypercare Support reacts to, and the measurement substrate that Measure SLO/SLA Adherence and Validate Production Quality rely on.
outputs: Configured alerting with routing and severities

tasks.name: Optimise Support & Tune Operations
tasks.purpose: Continuously optimise the hypercare support delivery and tune production operations — based on signals from the hypercare log, defect triage, user feedback and production telemetry — to reduce MTTR, improve user experience and stabilise the production system ahead of the hand-over to operations. Sits between Hypercare Support (reactive) and Pipeline Runbooks (durable documentation) as the deliberate improvement loop during the hypercare window.
outputs: Production-tuning log (what was changed and why)
Tuned alert thresholds (feeds Production Monitoring & Alerting)

tasks.name: Publish Pipeline Runbooks
tasks.purpose: Publish the pipeline-operations runbooks — how to run, debug, rollback, re-deploy, and hand-off the CD pipeline — as a durable artefact that survives beyond the hypercare window and the release wave. The runbooks are what operations inherits; they are also the first reference when the next Delivery Loop needs to refine pipeline behaviour. Distinct from Transformation's Operations Guide (program-level support), these runbooks are the technical pipeline reference.

tasks.name: Run Hypercare Support
tasks.purpose: Operate the project-side hypercare wrapper around the live solution. The customer's operations team runs the solution in production; the project team supports — triaging incidents, fixing critical defects fast, advising on operational decisions — for the agreed hypercare window. This is the bridge that lets accountability transfer to the customer without leaving them unsupported on day one.
outputs: Hypercare support delivered as a running capability. The outcome produces:

tasks.name: Ship Release to Production
tasks.purpose: Produce the **shipped Release** artefact — the Release Candidate now live in production — with published release notes, version manifest, release-linked audit trail and stakeholder communication. Execute Production Cutover is the *act*; this is the **artefact** that records the act and survives the release for audit, forensic analysis and customer-facing communication. The Release is the CD stream's final deliverable for the wave.

tasks.name: Track Production Defect Resolution
tasks.purpose: Track defect resolution velocity during the hypercare window — defects received, triaged, in progress, resolved and verified — calculating Mean Time to Restore (MTTR), backlog size, resolution rate and recurring root-cause patterns. The output is the operational scorecard for hypercare effectiveness and the Change-Failure-Rate + MTTR contribution to Track DORA Metrics. Pattern analysis here is the highest-value feedback into Refine CD Foundation and Refine Pipeline & Automation between waves.

tasks.name: Validate Production Quality
tasks.purpose: Continuously validate the quality of deployed artefacts in production during the hypercare window. The task goes beyond availability (covered by SLO/SLA adherence) to focus on functional and experiential quality — are the user flows working, is user-visible behaviour consistent with the pre-release baseline, are KPIs healthy? Regressions are escalated to Track Production Defect Resolution; persistent issues feed Hypercare Learnings and refine the CD Foundation for the next wave.
inputs: SLO / SLA monitors and pre-release baseline
